# Templates (.kcppt)

> Use ready-made KoboldCpp templates that download their models for you, load them from the launcher or command line, and create your own.

A `.kcppt` template holds launcher settings plus download links for the models. When you launch it, KoboldCpp downloads the files it needs and starts with those settings. Templates are the quickest way to a working setup, including for images, voice and music.

A template is a [config file](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/config-files/) meant for sharing. Most settings that depend on your PC are reset, so it works on other computers:

* The backend is chosen automatically for your hardware.
* GPU layers, threads, main GPU and tensor split are set to automatic.
* Passwords, SSL and Horde credentials are removed. **Use MMAP**, **Use mlock** and **Direct I/O** are turned off.
* Local file paths, **Download Dir:** and **Device Override** stay as they are. Check them before you share the template.

## Load a template from the launcher

1. Click **Get Help**.
2. Under "Or, Pick an Easy Template for Newbies", choose a category: **Newbie Templates** or **Popular Templates**.
3. Choose a template in the second dropdown.
4. Click **Load Template**. The launcher fills in the settings.
5. Click **Launch**. The download starts now and can take a while.

### Newbie templates

Sorted by how much graphics card memory (VRAM) they need:

| Prefix   | Recommended VRAM |
| -------- | ---------------- |
| LowSpec  | 6 GB             |
| MidSpec  | 12 GB            |
| HighSpec | 24 GB            |

| Template                               | For                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `LowSpec-Chatbot`, `MidSpec-Chatbot`   | Chat                           |
| `LowSpec-ImageGen`, `MidSpec-ImageGen` | Image generation               |
| `LowSpec-MusicGen`                     | Music generation               |
| `HighSpec-CodingAgent`                 | The KoboldCpp Agent for coding |
| `HighSpec-VideoGen`                    | Video generation               |

`LowSpec-Chatbot`, for example, loads Gemma 3 4B with vision, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and embeddings models, with a context size of 12288. Because that is below 16384, set KoboldAI Lite's **Context Size** to 12288 yourself; see [Context size](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/context-size/#koboldai-lite).

The templates live on Hugging Face: [newbie templates](https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/newbie-templates) and [popular templates](https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/popular-templates). The popular templates cover more models, such as Qwen3-VL 8B, Gemma 3 12B, and image and video models. More templates are in [koboldcpp/kcppt](https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/kcppt).

## Other ways to load a template

A `.kcppt` file loads like a `.kcpps` config:

* **Load Config** in the launcher.
* Drag the file onto the KoboldCpp exe.
* `--config` with a file name or an `https://` URL (`koboldcpp` stands for your KoboldCpp file; see [Command line](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/command-line/)):

Terminal

```sh
koboldcpp --config https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/newbie-templates/resolve/main/LowSpec-Chatbot.kcppt
```

On the command line, the backend is chosen automatically unless you add `--usecuda` or `--usevulkan`.

## Where downloads go

KoboldCpp downloads every model field that holds a web address when you launch, not when you load the template. The one exception is **Text Lora:**, which must be a local file.

* Files are saved in **Download Dir:** on the **Loaded Files** tab (`--downloaddir`). If that is empty, they go into the current working folder. When you double-click the exe, that is the folder the exe is in.
* A file that is already there is reused, so the next launch starts without downloading.
* For text models split into several parts (`-00001-of-00003.gguf` and so on), all parts are downloaded.
* KoboldCpp downloads with `aria2c` (bundled on Windows), `curl` or `wget`. If none of them works, it asks you to install one.

## Create a template

Set everything up in the launcher, then go to the **Extra** tab and click **Generate LaunchTemplate**. The file is saved as `.kcppt`. The chat adapter and preload story files are copied into the template, so it works without them.

For a template other people can use, enter web addresses instead of local file paths in the model fields, for example `https://huggingface.co/<user>/<repo>/resolve/main/<file>.gguf`. **HF Search** fills in addresses in this form.

From the command line, `--exporttemplate` does the same, but does not copy the chat adapter and preload story files:

Terminal

```sh
koboldcpp --model https://huggingface.co/<user>/<repo>/resolve/main/<file>.gguf --contextsize 16384 --exporttemplate mytemplate
```

To share a template or report a broken one, use the Discussions page of the [popular templates](https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/popular-templates) repository.

## Related

* [Choose a model](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/model/)
* [Config files (.kcpps)](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/config-files/)
* [Launcher tour](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/launcher-tour/)

# Connection and API problems

> Fixes for apps and devices that can't reach KoboldCpp, Remote Tunnel errors, broken pipes, 401 Unauthorized, busy server and payload errors.

KoboldCpp serves the chat UI and its API on port 5001 by default. When the model has loaded, the console shows the address:

```text
Please connect to custom endpoint at http://localhost:5001
```

## The browser does not open after loading

Open `http://localhost:5001` in any browser yourself.

* The launcher opens the browser only while **Launch Browser** is on (the default). On the command line, add `--launch`.
* On Linux, KoboldCpp tries `xdg-open` first, then Python's browser launcher.

## An app can't connect

1. Wait until the console shows `Please connect to custom endpoint at …`. The server starts only after the model has loaded.

2. Use the address for the app's API type:

   | The app speaks | Address                                                                |
   | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | KoboldAI API   | `http://localhost:5001`                                                |
   | OpenAI API     | `http://localhost:5001/v1`                                             |
   | Ollama API     | Start KoboldCpp with `--port 11434`, then use the app's Ollama default |

3. If you changed **Port:** (`--port`), use that port instead of 5001.

4. If you set a password, enter it in the app's API key field. See [below](#401-unauthorized).

See [Connect apps](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/connect-apps/).

## Other devices on my network can't connect

By default KoboldCpp accepts connections on all network interfaces. The console still prints `localhost`, which only works on the PC itself.

1. On the other device, use your PC's local network IP address: `http://<PC-IP>:5001`.
2. Allow KoboldCpp through the firewall on the PC. See [Remote access](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/remote-access/#same-network).
3. Check that **Host:** on the **Network** tab (`--host`) is empty. With `127.0.0.1`, only the PC itself can connect.

Set a password before other people can reach KoboldCpp. See [Passwords and security](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/passwords-and-security/).

## Remote Tunnel fails

```text
Error: Could not create cloudflare tunnel!
Remote Tunnel Failed!
```

**Remote Tunnel** (`--remotetunnel`) downloads the `cloudflared` program from GitHub on first use and then connects to Cloudflare. Both need internet access.

1. Check your internet connection, and that a firewall or antivirus does not block `cloudflared`.
2. Read the lines after `More Info:` in the console for the reason.
3. Restart KoboldCpp to try again.

`Could not create cloudflare tunnel!` appears when no link has arrived after about 15 seconds. If `Your remote tunnel is ready` follows later, the tunnel works.

Common causes:

| Cause                                                                                                                                                                       | Fix                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A firewall blocks `cloudflared`.                                                                                                                                            | Allow outgoing connections on port 7844 (TCP and UDP).                                                               |
| The download failed. The console shows `Could not find suitable download software, or all download methods failed.`                                                         | Check the internet connection. On Linux, install `curl`.                                                             |
| The saved `cloudflared` file is broken or too old.                                                                                                                          | Delete it (on a Mac also `cloudflared-darwin-amd64.tgz`). KoboldCpp downloads the latest version on the next launch. |
| **Download Dir:** on the **Loaded Files** tab (`--downloaddir`) is set. KoboldCpp then saves `cloudflared` there, but starts it from the folder KoboldCpp was started from. | Leave **Download Dir:** empty when you use **Remote Tunnel**.                                                        |
| On a Mac with Apple silicon, KoboldCpp downloads the Intel version of `cloudflared`, which needs Rosetta.                                                                   | Run `softwareupdate --install-rosetta`.                                                                              |

KoboldCpp saves `cloudflared` in the folder you start KoboldCpp from: `cloudflared.exe` on Windows, `cloudflared-linux-amd64` or `cloudflared-linux-arm64` on Linux, `cloudflared` on macOS. It reuses that file on every launch and does not update it. Cloudflare supports `cloudflared` versions up to one year old.

See [Remote access](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/remote-access/).

## "Network error" or "Broken pipe" during long prompts

The app shows `Network error when attempting to fetch resource`, or the console shows `[Errno 32] Broken pipe` and:

```text
Generate: The response could not be sent, maybe connection was terminated?
```

The app gave up waiting. This happens most often when a long prompt is processed again near the context limit.

1. Raise the timeout in your app, if it has one.
2. Make processing faster: put more layers on the graphics card. See [GPU not used or slow](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/gpu-and-speed/).
3. Raise **Context Size:**, so the prompt is processed again less often.

## 401 Unauthorized

```json
{"detail": {"error": "Unauthorized", "msg": "Authentication key is missing or invalid.", "type": "unauthorized"}}
```

KoboldCpp runs with a password (**Password:**, `--password`), and the request did not send it.

1. Enter the password in the app's API key field.
2. For your own requests, send the header `Authorization: Bearer <password>`.

KoboldCpp accepts the key only in the `Authorization` header. Apps built on the Anthropic SDK send `x-api-key`, which KoboldCpp does not accept.

Without the key, `/api/v1/model` shows the model name as `koboldcpp/protected-model`. That is expected. `/v1/models` still shows the real name.

## "Server is busy; please try again later."

KoboldCpp answers with HTTP 503. It handles one request at a time and queues the others, up to **Multiuser Queue:** (`--multiuser`, default 10) requests in total. This message means the queue is full, or queueing is off (`--multiuser 0`).

`--multiuser 0` keeps a queue anyway while an image, Whisper, TTS or embeddings model is loaded, or when **Parallel Requests:** is above 1. With [parallel requests](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/streaming/#advanced-parallel-requests), simple text requests can run at the same time.

1. Wait for the running requests to finish.
2. Leave **Multiuser Queue:** at its default, or raise it.

With **IP Rate Limiter (s):** (`--ratelimit`) set, too many requests from one address get `You are sending requests too quickly.` instead.

## "Payload is too big"

```text
Payload is too big. Max payload size is 32MB.
```

The request, for example with large images, is bigger than the limit. Raise **Max Req. Size (MB):** on the **Network** tab (`--maxrequestsize`, default 32).

## Advanced: SSL does not work

```text
Your SSL configuration is INVALID. SSL will not be used.
```

KoboldCpp then serves plain HTTP.

1. Give both files: **SSL Cert:** and **SSL Key:** (`--ssl cert.pem key.pem`), and check that both paths exist.
2. Use an unencrypted key file (no passphrase), in `.pem` format.

Certificate errors from the Horde worker, web search or MCP servers are about outgoing connections. **NoCertify Mode (Insecure)** (`--nocertify`) turns off those checks; it does not affect KoboldCpp's own certificate.

## Related

* [Connect apps](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/connect-apps/)
* [Remote access](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/remote-access/)
* [Passwords and security](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/passwords-and-security/)
* [Replies are cut short](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/output-quality/#replies-are-cut-short)

# GPU not used or generation slow

> Fixes for KoboldCpp ignoring your graphics card, "Unable to detect VRAM", CUDA errors, old NVIDIA cards and slow generation.

The console shows which backend KoboldCpp uses and how many layers went to the graphics card. Check it first when replies are slow.

## The graphics card is not used

```text
Unable to detect VRAM.
Auto Selected Default Backend (flag=0)
No GPU backend found, or could not automatically determine GPU layers. You may prefer to set layers manually.
```

`Auto Selected Default Backend` means KoboldCpp chose the CPU. When you don't pick a backend, KoboldCpp picks one itself:

* **CUDA** for an NVIDIA card with more than 3.5 GB of VRAM.
* Otherwise **Vulkan**, but only for a dedicated graphics card.
* Otherwise the CPU.

On Linux, KoboldCpp finds the graphics card with `nvidia-smi` (NVIDIA), `rocminfo` (AMD with ROCm) or `vulkaninfo`. For Vulkan, detection fails without `vulkaninfo`.

1. Pick the backend yourself: on **Quick Launch**, set **Backend:** to **Use CUDA** (NVIDIA) or **Use Vulkan** (any graphics card). On the command line: `--usecuda` or `--usevulkan`.
2. On Linux, install the `vulkan-tools` package.
3. If **Use CUDA** is missing from the list, you have the wrong file. See [below](#use-cuda-is-missing).
4. If KoboldCpp still puts no layers on the graphics card, set **GPU Layers:** to a number yourself (`--gpulayers 20`), and lower it if you run [out of memory](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/out-of-memory/).

On a Mac with Apple Silicon, `Unable to detect VRAM.` is normal. The Mac build puts all layers on the GPU automatically.

## "GPU layers is set, but a GPU backend was not selected"

```text
WARNING: GPU layers is set, but a GPU backend was not selected! GPU will not be used!
```

**Backend:** is set to a CPU option (**Use CPU** or `--usecpu`), so the layers stay on the CPU. Choose **Use CUDA** or **Use Vulkan** instead.

## "Use CUDA" is missing

The launcher only lists backends that your file contains. `koboldcpp-nocuda.exe` and `koboldcpp-linux-x64-nocuda` contain no CUDA. With `--usecuda` on the command line, they fall back to the CPU without an error.

1. For an NVIDIA card, download `koboldcpp.exe` (Linux: `koboldcpp-linux-x64`), or the `oldpc` file for an older card.
2. For AMD and Intel cards, use **Use Vulkan**. Every Windows and Linux file includes Vulkan.

See [Download KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/download/)

## Old NVIDIA card: "no device code compatible"

```text
ERROR: CUDA kernel mul_mat_vec has no device code compatible with CUDA arch 520
ggml-cuda was compiled without support for the current GPU architecture
```

The CUDA 12 builds support NVIDIA cards from compute capability 5.0. The `oldpc` builds use CUDA 11 and go down to compute capability 3.5.

1. Use `koboldcpp-oldpc.exe` or `koboldcpp-linux-x64-oldpc`.
2. If that fails too, use **Use Vulkan**.

See [CUDA versions and NVIDIA cards](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/releases/#advanced-cuda-versions-and-nvidia-cards).

## The first start with CUDA takes minutes

```text
Initializing CUDA/HIP, please wait, the following step may take a few minutes (only for first launch)...
```

On the first launch, CUDA prepares its code for your graphics card. This is normal and happens once. Wait for it to finish. On a PC with an RTX 3090, the first launch took 54 seconds and later launches about 10 seconds.

## "CUDA error" while generating

```text
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  current device: 0, in function … at …
```

Other variants include `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

1. Update your NVIDIA driver and [update KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/updating/).
2. With several graphics cards, try one card only: `--usecuda 0`.
3. Turn off **Use MMQ** (`--nommq`).
4. Switch to **Use Vulkan**.

## Replies are slow

1. Check that the graphics card is used (see [above](#the-graphics-card-is-not-used)). On NVIDIA, **Use CUDA** is faster than **Use Vulkan**. On Linux with an AMD card, try the [ROCm build](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/hardware/backends/#rocm).
2. Check how much of the model is on the graphics card. The more layers on the graphics card, the faster it runs. If only part fits, use a smaller quant or model, or lower **Context Size:** so more layers fit.
3. Keep **Use FlashAttention** on (the default).
4. For MoE models, leave **GPU Layers:** at `-1`. If the model does not fit, KoboldCpp then keeps part of the expert weights on the CPU and the rest on the graphics card by itself.
5. If the console processes the whole prompt again on every message, see [The whole prompt is processed again](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/output-quality/#the-whole-prompt-is-processed-again-on-every-message).

For example, Qwen3-VL-8B Q4\_K\_S on a PC with an RTX 3090 generated 82.0 tokens per second with all 37 layers on the graphics card, 45.2 with 30 layers, 23.9 with 20 and 11.9 on the CPU alone (prompt of about 1,000 tokens). Your numbers will differ.

See [GPU layers](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/hardware/gpu-layers/) and [GPU backends](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/hardware/backends/).

## Slow when the window is in the background (Windows)

On Intel processors of the 12th generation and newer, Windows can run a background KoboldCpp on the slower efficiency cores. Generation then slows down when the window is minimized or in the background.

1. Set **Threads:** on the **Hardware** tab (`--threads`) to the number of performance cores of your processor.
2. Turn on **Keep Foreground** (`--foreground`, Windows only). It brings the console to the front for every new request.

## Integrated graphics

KoboldCpp does not pick Vulkan automatically for integrated graphics. You can select **Use Vulkan** yourself. Compare its speed with the CPU alone and keep the faster one.

## Vulkan got slower, or stutters

Reports include slowdowns after playing games, which a restart fixed.

1. Restart KoboldCpp, or the PC.
2. Update your graphics driver.
3. Update KoboldCpp. If a new version got slower, try the previous one and report it.

## Advanced: several graphics cards

If CUDA errors appear only with several cards, test one card at a time with `--usecuda 0`, then `--usecuda 1`. Both CUDA and Vulkan support several cards.

See [Multiple GPUs](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/hardware/multi-gpu/).

## Related

* [Out of memory](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/out-of-memory/)
* [Release files and system requirements](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/releases/)
* [OS-specific problems](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/os-specific/)

# Model won't load

> Fixes for "Could not load text model", unknown model architecture, non-GGUF files, broken downloads, mismatched mmproj files and access violations.

KoboldCpp starts, but loading the model fails. The last error line is usually generic; the real cause is printed a few lines above it.

If loading stops with an "out of memory" or allocation error, see [Out of memory](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/out-of-memory/).

## "Could not load text model"

```text
Could not load text model: C:\models\mymodel.gguf
```

Sometimes also `failed to load model`. This is the final message for any load failure.

1. Scroll up in the console and find the first error above this line.
2. Look it up in the sections below or in [Out of memory](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/out-of-memory/).

## "unknown model architecture"

```text
llama_model_load: error loading model: unknown model architecture: '<name>'
```

Older versions print `error loading model architecture:` instead. Your KoboldCpp does not know this model's architecture, usually because the model is newer.

1. [Update KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/updating/) to the latest release.
2. If the latest release does not support it yet, wait for the next release, or try a [rolling build](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/releases/#advanced-rolling-builds). Rolling builds are updated automatically and can support a new model earlier, but may be unstable.

## "does not seem to be a GGUF file"

```text
WARNING: Selected Text Model does not seem to be a GGUF file! Are you sure you picked the right file?
```

The file name does not end in `.gguf`. KoboldCpp runs text models only as GGUF files (and legacy GGML `.bin` files). It cannot load `.safetensors` or PyTorch text models.

1. Download the GGUF version of the model. Search for the model name plus "GGUF" on Hugging Face.
2. Download one single `.gguf` file, not the whole repository. If the quant is split into parts (`-00001-of-00003.gguf`), download all parts and select the first. See [Choose a model](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/model/).

A model that exists only as safetensors must be converted to GGUF first. See [GGUF and quantization](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/models/gguf-and-quantization/).

## "all download methods failed"

```text
Could not find suitable download software, or all download methods failed. Please install aria2, curl, or wget.
```

KoboldCpp could not download a model file from a template or URL. The lines above it, such as `curl failed: …`, show why.

1. Check your internet connection.
2. On Linux, install `curl`, `wget` or `aria2`.
3. Launch again. Files that finished downloading are reused.

## The download is broken or incomplete

```text
llama_model_load: error loading model: read error: Input/output error
error: failed to read GGUF file
```

The file is damaged: the download stopped early, or the disk has read errors.

1. Compare the file size with the size on the download page.
2. Download the model again. If KoboldCpp downloaded it from a URL, delete that file first; otherwise KoboldCpp reuses it and prints `already exists, using existing file.`
3. If a fresh copy fails with `Input/output error` too, check the drive for errors, or move the model to another drive.

`--analyze mymodel.gguf` prints the file's metadata and tensors, which shows whether KoboldCpp can read it. In the launcher: **Analyze Model** on the **Extra** tab.

## The vision file (mmproj) fails to load

```text
error: failed to load mmproj model!
```

Loading can also crash without this message. A vision or audio projector (mmproj) works only with the model it was made for. For example, a Qwen mmproj cannot work with a Gemma model.

1. Use the mmproj made for your exact base model and size. A Gemma3 12B model needs the Gemma3 12B mmproj.
2. Ready-made projectors for popular models are in the [koboldcpp/mmproj](https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/mmproj/tree/main) repository.

See [Vision and audio input](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/vision/).

## Access violation while loading (Windows)

```text
OSError: exception: access violation reading 0x…
```

This has several causes, among them a graphics driver problem (reported with AMD cards on Vulkan), an unstable overclock, and non-ASCII characters in a path.

1. Update your graphics driver.
2. Try another backend. With an AMD card, try **Use Vulkan (Old CPU)**; otherwise try **Use CPU** to rule out the graphics card.
3. Lower **Context Size:** and try a small model to see if it loads at all.
4. Use folder and file names with plain ASCII characters. For image models, this can include your Windows user name; see [OS-specific problems](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/os-specific/#windows-a-user-name-or-folder-with-accented-letters).
5. If you overclock your CPU, GPU or RAM, test at stock speeds.

## Advanced: old GGML (.bin) models

GGML is the format before GGUF. KoboldCpp still loads it, but with limits:

```text
Warning: Your model may be an OUTDATED format (ver 3). Please reconvert it for better results!
Warning: Only GGUF models can use max context above 16k. Max context lowered to 16k.
```

Get a current GGUF version of the model instead. If a GGML model is detected as the wrong type, download a fresh copy; the file may be damaged or badly converted.

## Related

* [Out of memory](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/out-of-memory/)
* [Choose a model](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/model/)
* [Updating](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/updating/)

# OS-specific problems

> KoboldCpp problems that only happen on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android or Docker, from Windows 7 and Wayland file pickers to Gatekeeper.

Problems that affect every system are on the other Troubleshooting pages. This page collects the ones specific to one system.

## Windows: antivirus, SmartScreen or Smart App Control

See [Antivirus or Windows blocks or deletes the file](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/wont-start/#antivirus-or-windows-blocks-or-deletes-the-file).

## Windows: a user name or folder with accented letters

Paths with non-ASCII characters (umlauts, accents, other alphabets) can break model loading. Put KoboldCpp and your models in a folder with a plain ASCII path, for example `C:\mystuff`.

A Windows user name with such characters has been reported to make image models fail with an access violation, because KoboldCpp unpacks itself into the temporary folder inside the user profile. The latest release contains a fix for this that has not been confirmed yet. If image models still fail this way, a Windows user account with a plain ASCII name avoids the problem.

## Windows 7: KoboldCpp does not start

```text
DLL load failed while importing pyexpat
```

Or an error about a missing entry point such as `GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime`. The main builds use functions that exist only in Windows 8 and newer.

1. Use `koboldcpp-oldpc.exe`. Its libraries skip the Windows 8 functions.
2. For the `pyexpat` error, install the Windows update KB3063858.
3. If `msvcp140.dll` still reports `GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime`, one user fixed it this way: unpack KoboldCpp with **Unpack KoboldCpp To Folder** on the **Extra** tab, then replace the `msvcp140.dll` in that folder with an older version. Do not replace the one in the Windows system folders.

The third-party VxKex compatibility layer can make the main builds run. CUDA on Windows 7 is untested. See [Windows 7](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/windows/#advanced-windows-7).

## Windows: slow when the window is in the background

See [Slow when the window is in the background](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/gpu-and-speed/#slow-when-the-window-is-in-the-background-windows).

## Linux: "Permission denied"

The file is not executable yet.

Terminal

```sh
chmod +x koboldcpp-linux-x64
./koboldcpp-linux-x64
```

If the main build still fails on an older system, try `koboldcpp-linux-x64-oldpc`.

## Linux: "Unable to detect VRAM."

KoboldCpp finds your graphics card and its memory with `nvidia-smi` (NVIDIA), `rocminfo` (AMD with ROCm) or `vulkaninfo`. For Vulkan, install the `vulkan-tools` package, then restart KoboldCpp. See [The graphics card is not used](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/gpu-and-speed/#the-graphics-card-is-not-used).

## Linux: the file picker does nothing

Often on Wayland. The console may show:

```text
Zenity/YAD sanity check failed
```

1. Install `yad`. KoboldCpp prefers it over `zenity`.
2. Or turn on **Use Classic FilePicker** on the launcher's **Extra** tab.

## Linux: the launcher does not open

See ["Warning, GUI failed to start"](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/wont-start/#warning-gui-failed-to-start). On a server without a display, run KoboldCpp from the command line; see [Headless use](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/linux/#headless-use).

## Linux: the browser does not open

KoboldCpp tries `xdg-open` first, then Python's browser launcher. If neither works, open `http://localhost:5001` yourself.

## Linux: AMD graphics card

Use **Use Vulkan** in `koboldcpp-linux-x64-nocuda`. An experimental official ROCm build also exists; see [ROCm build for AMD on Linux](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/releases/#advanced-rocm-build-for-amd-on-linux).

## Linux: a self-built binary does not run on another PC

Since v1.122, `koboldcpp.sh` builds portable binaries only with `KCPP_PORTABLE=1`. See [Build from source](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/from-source/).

## macOS: nothing happens, or macOS blocks the file

The file is not executable yet, or Gatekeeper blocks it because it is not signed.

1. In Terminal, make it executable and run it:

   Terminal

   ```sh
   chmod +x koboldcpp-mac-arm64
   ./koboldcpp-mac-arm64
   ```

2. If macOS blocks it, allow it in **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, then run it again.

See [macOS](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/macos/).

## macOS: "Unable to detect VRAM."

This is normal on Apple Silicon. KoboldCpp puts all layers on the GPU (Metal) anyway:

```text
MacOS detected: Auto GPU layers set to maximum
```

## macOS: Intel Mac

There is no ready-made file for Intel Macs, and they are poorly supported. You can [build from source](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/from-source/#macos).

## macOS: run without Metal

`--failsafe` switches to a CPU-only library that uses Apple's Accelerate framework instead of Metal.

## Android: "Illegal instruction"

Some devices crash with `Illegal instruction`. Compile with `make LLAMA_PORTABLE=1`, which turns off ARM-specific instructions. See [Android (Termux)](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/android/).

## Android: packages fail to install

Run `termux-change-repo` and pick another mirror, then run the setup again.

## Docker: very slow

The Docker image detects processor features only roughly and can fall back to the failsafe libraries, which are extremely slow. Choose the backend yourself, for example `--usecuda` or `--usevulkan` in `KCPP_ARGS`. See [Docker](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/colab-docker/#docker-experts).

## Related

* [KoboldCpp won't start](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/wont-start/)
* [Windows](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/windows/), [Linux](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/linux/), [macOS](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/macos/), [Android (Termux)](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/android/)

# Out of memory errors (VRAM and RAM)

> Fixes for KoboldCpp running out of VRAM or RAM, including cudaMalloc failed, ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory and being killed while loading.

A model needs memory for its weights (roughly the file size), for the context (the KV cache, which grows with **Context Size:**) and for working buffers. When that is more than your graphics card or PC has, loading fails.

See [How much memory a model needs](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/models/memory/).

## "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" (NVIDIA)

```text
ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating … MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
```

Followed by one of these:

```text
unable to allocate CUDA0 buffer
failed to allocate buffer for kv cache
failed to allocate compute pp buffers
```

The layers on the graphics card, the context and the buffers together need more VRAM than is free. Try these in order, and relaunch after each:

1. Leave **GPU Layers:** at `-1` (`--gpulayers -1`). KoboldCpp then fits as many layers as possible into VRAM. If you set a number yourself, lower it.

2. Lower **Context Size:** (`--contextsize`). The default is 16384. See [Context size](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/context-size/).

3. Close other programs that use the graphics card. KoboldCpp warns you about them:

   ```text
   Note: KoboldCpp has detected that a significant amount of GPU VRAM (… MB) is currently used by another application.
   ```

4. Quantize the context: set **Quantize KV Cache:** on the **Context** tab to `q8_0`, or `q4_0` for more savings (`--quantkv q8_0`). Keep **Use FlashAttention** on; without it, only part of the cache is quantized, and it can even use more VRAM.

5. Use a smaller quant of the model, or a smaller model. See [Choosing a quant](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/models/gguf-and-quantization/).

6. Lower **Batch Size:** on the **Hardware** tab (`--batchsize`, default 512).

7. As a last resort, `--lowvram` keeps the context in system RAM. It is slow and not recommended.

More options: [GPU layers](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/hardware/gpu-layers/) and [Saving VRAM](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/hardware/saving-vram/).

## "ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory" (Vulkan)

```text
ggml_vulkan: Device memory allocation of size … failed.
vk::Device::allocateMemory: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate Vulkan0 buffer of size …
```

The Vulkan backend ran out of VRAM. The fixes are the same as for [NVIDIA](#cudamalloc-failed-out-of-memory-nvidia): put fewer layers on the graphics card, lower the context size, close other programs.

Some Vulkan devices cannot allocate more than about 2 GB in one piece, even with more VRAM free. For image generation, these flags help: `--sdvaeauto`, `--sdquant`, and `--sdconvdirect vaeonly`.

See [Image generation](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/image-generation/).

## KoboldCpp is killed while loading

The console shows `Terminated`, or KoboldCpp ends without an error, while system memory (RAM) is almost full. The model does not fit into RAM.

1. Use a smaller quant or a smaller model.
2. Close other programs.
3. Turn on **Use MMAP** (`--usemmap`). The system then reads the model file from disk as needed, instead of loading it all into RAM first.
4. Lower **Context Size:**.

## Advanced: "not enough space in the scratch memory"

Messages like `not enough space in the context's memory pool` or `scratch memory` come from old GGML models and very old versions. Current versions show the CUDA or Vulkan errors above. Update KoboldCpp and use a GGUF model.

## Related

* [Context size](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/context-size/)
* [GPU not used or slow](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/gpu-and-speed/)
* [Your first model: how much memory you need](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/models/memory/)

# Bad or strange output

> Fixes for gibberish output, a model that never stops, the AI replying as you, cut-off replies, ignored images and context warnings in KoboldCpp.

The model loads, but its replies are wrong. Most settings on this page are in KoboldAI Lite's settings, not in the launcher.

## The AI writes gibberish

Replies are random characters, repeated symbols or nonsense words. Known causes are graphics driver bugs (often AMD cards with Vulkan), a badly converted model file, and bugs in a KoboldCpp version with specific models.

1. Update your graphics driver.
2. Try another backend. With AMD on Vulkan, try **Use Vulkan (Old CPU)**. To rule out the graphics card, try **Use CPU**.
3. Download the model again, from a well-known uploader.
4. [Update KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/updating/).
5. Try a different **Batch Size:** on the **Hardware** tab (`--batchsize`).
6. Turn off **Use FlashAttention** (`--noflashattention`).
7. If you set a custom RoPE configuration, remove it. The default scales automatically.

If a model still produces gibberish, report it with the model name and your settings.

## The AI never stops, or keeps rambling

The model's end token (EOS) is banned, or the instruct format does not match the model. The reply then runs until the output length is used up.

1. In KoboldAI Lite, open **Settings** > **Misc**. Under **Advanced Settings**, set **EOS token ban** to **Auto** (the default) or **Unban**.
2. In instruct mode, check that the instruct tags match the model. Lite's default placeholder tags adapt to the model automatically.

The old `--unbantokens` flag no longer exists; KoboldCpp exits with `unrecognized arguments` if you pass it.

## The AI replies as me in chat mode

The model writes your lines as well as its own.

1. Retry the reply.
2. In KoboldAI Lite, open **Settings** > **General** and turn off **Allow multiline replies**.
3. Use a model that was trained for chat.
4. Check the character card and the start of the chat: consistent, correctly spelled names and a few good example messages help.

## Replies are cut short

In other apps that use the API, replies stop after a fixed length when the app does not send a length. KoboldCpp then uses its default, **Default Gen Amt:** on the **Context** tab (`--defaultgenamt`, 2048 tokens). It is capped at half the context size.

1. Set the reply length (`max_tokens` or "max length") in your app.
2. Or raise **Default Gen Amt:**, and raise **Context Size:** if half of it is below what you need.
3. Check that **Prompt Limit:** (`--genlimit`) is not set; it caps every reply.

In KoboldAI Lite chat mode, turning off **Allow multiline replies** (**Settings** > **General**) also shortens replies to one line.

## Badly formatted replies over the Chat Completions API

```text
Chat template heuristics failed to identify chat completions format. Alpaca will be used.
```

KoboldCpp could not tell which chat format the model uses and fell back to Alpaca, which may not match.

1. Turn on **Use Jinja** on the launcher's **Context** tab (`--jinja`). KoboldCpp then uses the chat template stored in the model file.
2. Or pick the format yourself: **Chat Adapter:** on the **Loaded Files** tab, with **Pick Premade** (`--chatcompletionsadapter`).

See [Chat formatting](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/overview/#chat-formatting).

## The whole prompt is processed again on every message

Normally KoboldCpp reuses the processed text and, when the context is full, shifts it (ContextShift). On models with sliding window attention (SWA), such as Gemma 3, SWA is on by default and turns ContextShift off:

```text
SWA Mode is ENABLED!
Note that using SWA Mode cannot be used with Context Shifting!
```

1. Keep **Use FastForwarding** and **Use ContextShift** on (the defaults).
2. To get ContextShift back on an SWA model, turn off **Allow SWA** on the **Context** tab (`--noswa`). This uses much more memory for the context.
3. **Parallel Requests:** above 1 also turns ContextShift off. Set it to 1 if you don't need parallel requests.

## The AI ignores my image or audio

```text
Warning: Media excluded - Context size too low or not enough mtmd tokens! (needed …)
Media will be IGNORED! You probably want to relaunch with a larger context size!
```

The image or audio did not fit into the context. Relaunch with a larger **Context Size:**. Long audio clips need a lot of context.

Without a vision file (mmproj) loaded, the model cannot see images at all. See [Vision and audio input](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/vision/).

## Warnings about the context size

```text
Warning! Request max_context_length=32768 exceeds allocated context size of 16384. It will be reduced to fit.
Warning: You are trying to generate text with max_length (10000) near or exceeding max_context_length limit (16384).
```

Your app asked for more context than KoboldCpp reserved at launch, or for a reply almost as long as the whole context. Most of the story is then cut off, and replies lose coherence.

1. Relaunch with a larger **Context Size:** (`--contextsize`). An app's context setting cannot go above the launch value.
2. Or lower the context size and reply length in your app.

See [Context size](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/context-size/).

## "Quantized KV was used without flash attention"

```text
Warning: Quantized KV was used without flash attention! This is NOT RECOMMENDED!
```

With **Use FlashAttention** off, a quantized context cache (**Quantize KV Cache:**, `--quantkv`) only partly works and can even use more VRAM. Turn **Use FlashAttention** back on, or set **Quantize KV Cache:** to `f16`.

## Advanced: sampler settings

Extreme sampler values also produce bad output. KoboldAI Lite's defaults are a good reset point:

| Setting            | Lite default      |
| ------------------ | ----------------- |
| Temperature        | 0.75              |
| Repetition penalty | 1.05              |
| Top-P              | 0.92              |
| Sampler order      | `[6,0,1,3,4,2,5]` |

An API request with an invalid order logs `ERROR: sampler_order must be a list of integers`.

See [KoboldAI Lite](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/lite/).

## Related

* [Context size](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/context-size/)
* [GPU not used or slow](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/gpu-and-speed/)
* [Connection and API problems](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/connection/)

# Won't start or closes straight away

> Fixes for KoboldCpp crashing or closing at startup, antivirus blocks, WinError 1114, Illegal instruction, a blank console and a port in use.

Most start problems print an error in the console window. If the window closes too fast to read it, start with the first section.

## The window closes straight away

KoboldCpp crashed, and the console window closed before you could read the error. KoboldCpp writes no log file, so run it from a terminal, where the message stays on screen.

* Windows

  1. Open Command Prompt.

  2. Go to the folder with KoboldCpp and start it:

     Command Prompt

     ```sh
     cd C:\mystuff
     koboldcpp.exe
     ```

* Linux

  1. Open a terminal.

  2. Go to the folder with KoboldCpp and start it:

     Terminal

     ```sh
     cd ~/Downloads
     ./koboldcpp-linux-x64
     ```

* macOS

  1. Open Terminal.

  2. Go to the folder with KoboldCpp and start it:

     Terminal

     ```sh
     cd ~/Downloads
     ./koboldcpp-mac-arm64
     ```

Look up the error on this page or in [Model won't load](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/model-wont-load/). Errors from the launcher itself appear in a message box instead.

## Antivirus or Windows blocks or deletes the file

What you may see:

* Microsoft Defender or another antivirus reports a trojan, for example:

  ```text
  Trojan:Win32/Sabsik.FL.A!ml
  Trojan:Script/Wacatac.B!ml
  ```

* "Windows protected your PC" (SmartScreen).

* The exe shrinks to 0 bytes, or this error appears:

  ```text
  Failed to extract koboldcpp_vulkan_noavx2.dll: decompression resulted in return code -3!
  ```

The exe is not code-signed and unpacks its libraries into a temporary folder when it starts. Heuristic and machine-learning scanners flag this. For a file from the official releases, it is a false positive.

1. Check that the file came from the [official GitHub releases](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest). See [Staying safe](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/staying-safe/).
2. For SmartScreen, click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
3. For an antivirus, add the file to its exceptions and report the false positive to the vendor.
4. If the file was quarantined, shrank or fails to extract, download it again.

**Smart App Control** has no exception list. It blocks KoboldCpp for as long as it is turned on.

## "DLL initialization routine failed" (WinError 1114)

```text
OSError: [WinError 1114] A dynamic link library (DLL) initialization routine failed
```

This appears after `Initializing dynamic library: …`. Related errors are `0xc0000142` and `Failed to execute script 'koboldcpp' due to unhandled exception!`.

Common causes: the processor lacks AVX2, the NVIDIA driver is too old for the CUDA 12 build, or an antivirus removed a library.

1. If your processor or NVIDIA card is older, use `koboldcpp-oldpc.exe` (CUDA 11, needs only AVX1). See [Download KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/download/)
2. Otherwise, update your NVIDIA driver. `nvidia-smi` in Command Prompt shows the installed driver.
3. Rule out your antivirus: download the file again and add an exception.

`Failed to execute script 'koboldcpp'` also follows other errors, such as a [port in use](#port-5001-already-appears-to-be-in-use). Read the lines above it.

## "Illegal instruction" or `0xc000001d`

```text
Illegal instruction (core dumped)
```

On Windows the error code is `0xc000001d`. Your processor lacks an instruction set (AVX2 or AVX) that the selected backend needs. KoboldCpp normally detects this and picks a compatible mode, but a backend chosen by hand or saved in a config file overrides the detection.

1. In the launcher, set **Backend:** to an option marked **(Old CPU)**, for example **Use CPU (Old CPU)** or **Use Vulkan (Old CPU)**. On the command line, add `--noavx2`.
2. If it still crashes, your processor has no AVX either. Use **Failsafe Mode (Older CPU)** (`--failsafe`), which uses no graphics card.
3. To use a graphics card on a processor without AVX, download the `oldpc` file and choose **Use Vulkan (Older CPU)** (`--usevulkan --failsafe`).

See [Processor requirements](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/releases/#processor-avx2-avx-no-avx) for which build contains which mode. On Android, see [OS-specific problems](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/os-specific/#android-illegal-instruction).

## The console stays blank and the launcher never opens

The exe could not unpack itself into the temporary folder. It needs about 1 GB of free space on the system drive, and an antivirus can block the unpacking.

1. Free up space on the system drive.
2. Check your antivirus (see [above](#antivirus-or-windows-blocks-or-deletes-the-file)).
3. Try the smaller `koboldcpp-nocuda.exe`.
4. Or unpack KoboldCpp once and start it from the unpacked folder; see [Unpack for faster startup](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/windows/#advanced-unpack-for-faster-startup).

## "Port 5001 already appears to be in use"

```text
Warning: Port 5001 already appears to be in use by another program.
OSError: Cannot start the server: no socket could bind.
```

Another KoboldCpp, or another program, already uses the port. KoboldCpp loads the whole model first and fails only when it starts the server.

1. Close the other KoboldCpp window.
2. Or use a different port: **Port:** on the **Network** tab, or `--port 5002`.

To let a new KoboldCpp replace a running one automatically, start both with **SingleInstance Mode** (**Admin** tab) or `--singleinstance`. The new instance then asks the old one on the same port to shut down.

## "Warning, GUI failed to start"

```text
Warning, GUI failed to start: Reason: no display name and no $DISPLAY environment variable
File selection GUI unsupported.
customtkinter python module required!
```

The launcher could not open a window. Usually there is no display (a server or SSH session), or, when you run from source, the `tkinter` or `customtkinter` Python module is missing.

1. Start KoboldCpp without the launcher by giving it a model: `--model mymodel.gguf`, or a config file with `--config mysettings.kcpps`.
2. When running from source, install `tkinter` and `customtkinter` to get the launcher back.

`--skiplauncher` on its own does not help: without `--model` it exits with an error. See [Headless use](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/linux/#headless-use).

## "Cannot find text model file" or "config file invalid or not found"

```text
Cannot find text model file: C:\models\mymodel.gguf
Specified kcpp config file invalid or not found.
No gguf model or kcpps file was selected. Exiting.
```

The path is wrong, or the file has moved.

1. Check the path and file name. Put paths with spaces in quotes on the command line.
2. Use folder and file names with plain ASCII characters. Umlauts and other accented letters in a model path can break loading.
3. For a config file, open it with **Load Config** in the launcher to check it.

## "No Backends Available!" (running from source)

```text
KoboldCPP couldn't locate any backends to use (i.e Default, Vulkan, CUDA).
```

You started `koboldcpp.py` from source code without compiling it first. Run `make` in the folder; see [Build from source](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/from-source/).

## Problems on one system only

* Windows 7, Linux permissions and file pickers, macOS security settings, Android: [OS-specific problems](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/os-specific/).
* The model fails to load after KoboldCpp starts: [Model won't load](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/model-wont-load/).

# Download KoboldCpp

> Download KoboldCpp for Windows, Linux or macOS from the official GitHub releases: one file, no installer. Pick the file for your graphics card.

KoboldCpp is one file. There is no installer. Pick your system, then click the file for your graphics card. Not sure which card you have? See [below](#which-graphics-card-do-i-have). Every link goes to the [latest official release on GitHub](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest).

* Windows

  [NVIDIA graphics card](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp.exe)koboldcpp.exe

  [AMD or Intel graphics, or none](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp-nocuda.exe)koboldcpp-nocuda.exe, a much smaller download

  [Older PC](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp-oldpc.exe)koboldcpp-oldpc.exe, for older devices, if the others crash at start

* Linux

  [NVIDIA graphics card](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp-linux-x64)koboldcpp-linux-x64

  [AMD or Intel graphics, or none](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp-linux-x64-nocuda)koboldcpp-linux-x64-nocuda, a much smaller download

  [Older PC](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp-linux-x64-oldpc)koboldcpp-linux-x64-oldpc, if the others crash at start

* macOS

  [Apple Silicon (M-series)](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest/download/koboldcpp-mac-arm64)koboldcpp-mac-arm64

  Intel Macs have no ready-made file. See [Build from source](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/from-source/#macos).

Beware of fake sites

You should **ONLY** trust official downloads from the release binaries linked here and the official KoboldCpp Github at <https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest>.

## Which graphics card do I have?

On Windows, the Task Manager shows it.

1. Launch **Windows Task Manager** with keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Alt+Del or Ctrl+Shift+Esc.
2. Click **Performance** tab.
3. Click **GPU** in the list on the left. The card's name is at the top right. **Dedicated GPU memory** is the card's own memory, its **VRAM**. It determines what models work well for your system. [![Windows Task Manager showing GPU name](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/windows-task-manager.BdMTKDqZ_Z2ckVSL.webp)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/windows-task-manager.BdMTKDqZ.png)

On Linux, `lspci | grep -iE 'vga|3d'` shows the card's name, and `nvidia-smi` shows an NVIDIA card's memory. On a Mac with Apple Silicon, the graphics chip uses the Mac's main memory.

Pick the download suited to your system and GPU card.

All files and what each contains: [Release files and system requirements](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/releases/).

# Getting started with KoboldCpp

> A beginner's guide to KoboldCpp with screenshots: download one file, start it, choose a model and chat in your browser. No installer, no account.

KoboldCpp runs AI models on your own computer. This guide takes you from download to your first chat in four steps. You don't need to know anything about AI.

1. [**Download KoboldCpp**](https://koboldcpp.net/download/): one file from GitHub. There is no installer.

2. [**Start KoboldCpp**](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/start/): open the file. A settings window, the launcher, appears.

3. [**Choose a model and launch**](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/model/): the model is the AI itself. The launcher can download one for you.

4. [**Chat**](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/chat/): KoboldAI Lite opens in your web browser.

## What you need

* A computer with Windows, Linux, or a Mac with an Apple Silicon (M-series) chip.
* Up to about 8 GB of free disk space for KoboldCpp and a beginner model.
* A graphics card is not required. With one, replies come much faster.

[Next Step](https://koboldcpp.net/download/)

Stuck at any point? See [Help](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/help/). Everything beyond the basics is in the [wiki](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/).

# Chat with your model in KoboldAI Lite

> When the model has loaded, KoboldCpp opens KoboldAI Lite in your browser. Pick a look and send your first message.

When the model has loaded, your browser opens KoboldAI Lite, the chat app built into KoboldCpp. If it doesn't open, go to `http://localhost:5001` yourself.

1. Choose a look and click **Set UI**. **Corpo UI** looks like a typical chat app. You can change it later in **Settings**.

   [![KoboldAI Lite welcome dialog with Classic, Aesthetic and Corpo UI styles](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/lite-choose-style.BqgEN4DV_Z194BYd.webp)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/lite-choose-style.BqgEN4DV.png)

2. Type a message and click the arrow button to send it (in Classic UI: **Submit**).

   [![A first message and the model's reply in KoboldAI Lite](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/lite-first-chat._0bc6cLK_1JB7Cb.webp)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/lite-first-chat._0bc6cLK.png)

Here are all the WebUIs bundled with KoboldCpp for various tasks (assuming port 5001) http\://localhost:5001 - KoboldAI Lite WebUI: Versatile multi-purpose WebUI for chatting/roleplay and basic image generation. http\://localhost:5001/lcpp - llama.cpp WebUI: Ported from llama.cpp and mimics ChatGPT. Use if you prefer a more "Assistant" feel. http\://localhost:5001/sdui - Stable-UI: A dedicated image generation WebUI. Use this if you are generating or editing images or videos. http\://localhost:5001/musicui - MusicUI: A dedicate music generation WebUI. Use this to generate music, you can also use this to generate speech with TTS models.

That's it: everything runs on your computer. To stop KoboldCpp, close its console window.

## Next time

In the launcher, **Save Config** saves your settings to a `.kcpps` file. Next time, click **Load Config**, pick that file and click **Launch**.

# Help and next steps

> Quick fixes for the most common KoboldCpp problems for beginners, where to ask for help, and what to try after your first chat.

Many problems show an error message in the console window. Keep it open and read it.

## Common problems

**Windows or your antivirus blocks the file.** For files from the [official releases](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest) this is a false alarm: the file is not signed. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**, or allow the file in your antivirus. [More](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/windows/#smartscreen-and-antivirus-warnings)

**The window closes straight away.** Start KoboldCpp from a Command Prompt (Windows) or a terminal, so the error stays on screen. On an older PC, try the `oldpc` file. [More](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/wont-start/)

**"Out of memory", or a crash while loading.** Pick a smaller model or the `LowSpec` template, and close other programs that use the graphics card. [More](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/out-of-memory/)

**Replies are very slow.** Check that **Backend:** on **Quick Launch** shows **Use CUDA** (NVIDIA) or **Use Vulkan** (AMD, Intel), not **Use CPU**. If **Use CUDA** is missing on an NVIDIA PC, you have the `nocuda` file; [download](https://koboldcpp.net/download/) `koboldcpp.exe` instead. [More](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/gpu-and-speed/)

**The model doesn't load.** Use one `.gguf` file, and download it again if the download was cut short. Newer model types need the latest KoboldCpp. [More](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/troubleshooting/model-wont-load/)

**Nothing happens on macOS.** Run it from Terminal as shown in [Start KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/getting-started/start/), and allow it in **System Settings → Privacy & Security**. [More](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/macos/)

## Ask for help

Ask on the [KoboldAI Discord](https://koboldai.org/discord) or in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/discussions). Found a bug? [Report it on GitHub](https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/issues). Copy the error from the console window into your message.

## What to try next

* [Connect SillyTavern and other apps](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/api/connect-apps/)
* [Make pictures](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/image-generation/)
* [Talk to it](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/speech-to-text/) and [hear replies read aloud](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/features/text-to-speech/)
* [Let it remember more of the conversation](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/settings/context-size/)
* [Update KoboldCpp](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/updating/)

Everything else is in the [wiki](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/).

# Choose a model and launch

> Pick your first AI model for KoboldCpp: a newbie template that downloads everything for you, or one of four recommended model files. Then click Launch.

KoboldCpp doesn't come with an AI model; you add one. A model is one large file that ends in `.gguf`.

## The easy way: a newbie template

A template fills in the launcher for you and downloads the model when you click **Launch**. The `Chatbot` templates also add voice input, read-aloud and picture understanding.

1. In the launcher, click **Get Help** and the dropdown **Newbie Templates**.

2. Pick a template for your graphics card's memory (VRAM; [how to check](https://koboldcpp.net/download/#which-graphics-card-do-i-have)):

   * Chat with the AI:

     * `LowSpec-Chatbot`: recommend for 6 GB VRAM or no GPU. Chat or roleplay, also has vision, speech generation and voice recognition capabilities.
     * `MidSpec-Chatbot`: recommend for 12 GB VRAM or more. Chat or roleplay, also has vision, speech generation and voice recognition capabilities.

   * Generating Images:

     * `LowSpec-ImageGen`: recommend for 6 GB VRAM or no GPU for creating and editing AI images. Launch the dedicated SDUI when prompted.
     * `LowSpec-ImageGen`: recommend for 12 GB VRAM for creating and editing AI images. Launch the dedicated SDUI when prompted.

   * Generating Music:
     * `LowSpec-MusicGen`: recommend for 6 GB VRAM or no GPU for generating music. Launch the dedicated MusicUI when prompted. You can add an extra LLM model for better lyrics generation.

   * Agent and Coding:

     * `LowSpec-CodingAgent`: recommend for 6 GB VRAM or no GPU for coding tasks. Launches an agentic terminal.
     * `MidSpec-CodingAgent`: recommend for 12 GB VRAM for coding tasks. Launches an agentic terminal.

3. Click **Load Template**.

   [![The Help Menu: Newbie Templates, the LowSpec-Chatbot template and the Load Template button](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/launcher-get-help.Cjkf-1Bn_ZvSCgI.webp)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/launcher-get-help.Cjkf-1Bn.png)

## Or: download one model file

These are some basic models that work in KoboldCpp. Click one to download it. For more models, visit [Huggingface](https://huggingface.co/models?library=gguf).

[Qwen3-VL-8B](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_S.gguf)The best all-rounder · 4.8 GB

[L3-8B-Stheno-v3.2](https://huggingface.co/bartowski/L3-8B-Stheno-v3.2-GGUF/resolve/main/L3-8B-Stheno-v3.2-Q4_K_S.gguf)Creative writing and roleplay · 4.7 GB

[Gemma 3 4B](https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/gemma-3-4b-it-GGUF/resolve/main/gemma-3-4b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf)Small and fast, for weaker PCs · 2.5 GB

[PicX Real](https://huggingface.co/koboldcpp/imgmodel/resolve/main/picx_real_q8_0.gguf)Makes pictures · 1.8 GB

In the launcher, click **Browse** next to **GGUF Text Model:** and select the file. PicX Real is an image model: it goes into **Image Model** on the **Image Gen** tab instead.

## Launch

Click **Launch**.

[![GGUF Text Model field with a model selected (1) and the Launch button (2)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/launcher-model-launch.pqsOrZko_ZUEX0N.webp)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/launcher-model-launch.pqsOrZko.png)

The launcher closes, and the console window shows the model loading. With a template, it first downloads the files, which can take a while. The next launch reuses them.

# Start KoboldCpp for the first time

> Open the KoboldCpp file on Windows, Linux or macOS, get past the first-start warning, and reach the launcher.

Put the file you downloaded in a folder of its own, for example `C:\mystuff` on Windows. Models that KoboldCpp downloads for you are saved next to it.

* Windows

  Double-click the file. A black console window opens, then the launcher.

  If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This is expected: the file is not signed. If your antivirus removes the file, see [SmartScreen and antivirus warnings](https://koboldcpp.net/docs/install/windows/#smartscreen-and-antivirus-warnings).

* Linux

  Open a terminal in the folder with the file, make it executable and run it. This example uses the NVIDIA file; use your file's name:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  cd ~/Downloads
  chmod +x koboldcpp-linux-x64
  ./koboldcpp-linux-x64
  ```

* macOS

  Open Terminal, make the file executable and run it:

  Terminal

  ```sh
  cd ~/Downloads
  chmod +x koboldcpp-mac-arm64
  ./koboldcpp-mac-arm64
  ```

  The first time, macOS says it could not verify the file. Click **Done**, then open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**. Run the file again and confirm.

The launcher opens on the **Quick Launch** tab. KoboldCpp picks the **Backend:** for your hardware, and the other defaults generally work, so leave them as they are.

[![The KoboldCpp launcher on the Quick Launch tab with default settings](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/launcher-start.Dobnsw9D_2mAU0B.webp)](https://koboldcpp.net/_astro/launcher-start.Dobnsw9D.png)

Keep the console window (or terminal) open while you use KoboldCpp. Closing it stops KoboldCpp.
